lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 30
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The End of Choosing
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City stopped pretending to be passive.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It began with the water.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They had grown used to the shallow black pools that appeared in chambers and along corridors—one more unpleasant feature of a place that seemed to hold a personal grudge against human comfort. Then the water started moving with intent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When BAH-lahg knelt to refill a waterskin, the surface rippled toward him before he touched it. Small, deliberate rings traveled uphill against the natural slope of the stone. He froze with the skin still in his hand.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Did you see that?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun had already turned.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It moved.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Water does that.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Not toward a man before he touches it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one answered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They pressed on, keeping clear of the black pools. A few minutes later BAH-lahg muttered under his breath about the City, the dead, and the questionable intelligence of anyone who walked willingly into a place that had been buried for thousands of years. His voice was low, barely more than breath.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It carried strangely down the corridor.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A moment later it came back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not as an echo. The voice was stretched thin and wet, distorted in a way that made Zeek's skin crawl, but the words were unmistakably BAH-lahg's, and they came from somewhere ahead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stopped walking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A second repetition rose from behind. A third bled out of the darkness to their left.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stepped toward the nearest wall and held her palm just short of the oily stone.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It's recording us. Or learning how we sound when we're afraid.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I wasn't afraid,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wall repeated him, word for word, in a voice that had learned his cadence better than he liked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo laughed once, short and without humor.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: The City disagrees.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them the water rippled again—and this time it spoke in Zeek's voice.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: En-HEH-doo.
lines.note: CITY MIMIC of Zik's voice from the water: wet, stretched, wrong.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She spun. Nothing stood behind her. The black surface trembled once and went still. The mark under Zeek's wrappings gave a slow, answering pulse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not like that the City had borrowed his voice. He liked even less that it had known exactly whose name to say with it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They moved faster after that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statues came next.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first stood at the mouth of a side passage they had not noticed before. It was taller than any of them, carved from the same dull, oily stone as the walls, its face blank except for the spiral-drop symbol cut deep into the brow. It did not move when they approached. It simply occupied the space with the absolute patience of something that had nowhere else to be.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tested the floor in front of it out of habit. His body still knew the sequence even if the conscious lesson was gone. The stone held.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They passed it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When Zeek looked back, the statue had turned its head to watch them leave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one commented. Commenting would have required deciding what the movement meant.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second statue waited at a junction three turns later. The third appeared in a doorway that had been empty when they last checked. By the fourth they had stopped counting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City was no longer content to wait behind thresholds. It was rearranging the board.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They made camp in a chamber that offered two exits and no pools. BAH-lahg took first watch. Ninsun wrote until the stylus refused another line and then sat staring at the blank space as though the parchment itself had begun to withhold cooperation. En-HEH-doo sat with her back to the wall, the figurine in her lap, looking at it the way a person studies an object whose purpose belongs to someone else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek opened the journal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The map had shifted again. The upper layers—the desert, the outpost, the first staircase—had faded almost to invisibility. In their place the ink had thickened into a denser network of descending lines. At the center of the densest tangle the spiral-drop appeared complete, larger than any they had seen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beneath it, in a hand that was neither his father's nor his own:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THE CITY IS TIRED OF WAITING.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He closed the book before anyone else could see the words.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Sometime after the others had gone quiet he heard water moving in the dark. When he opened his eyes the statue was standing in the entrance, taller than the doorway, its head forced down beneath the stone arch to fit. The spiral-drop crown sat on its brow. Its carved face pointed straight at him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It did not attack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It waited.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's hand went to his knife. The statue did not shift. He looked past it to the doorway, then back at the stone face, then down at the mark on his palm. The mark knocked once, soft and deliberate, against the inside of his skin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statue's head turned—not toward Zeek, toward the corridor. Toward the way that led deeper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun rose slowly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It wants us to follow.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then we go the other way,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said, already moving.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They tried. The wall behind them opened onto a corridor that had not existed a breath earlier. It led—of course it led—straight back toward the statue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg swore under his breath.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo stood, picked up the figurine, studied it with the same blank expression she had worn since the vision, and tucked it into her pack.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Why are you still taking that?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo looked down at it as though the answer might be written somewhere on the gold.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I don't know.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That silenced them faster than an argument would have.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statue stepped aside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beyond it the corridor sloped downward into darkness that did not end in torchlight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City had stopped offering choices.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now it was herding them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statue did not move when BAH-lahg shoved it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It did not even shift. It felt less like rock and more like part of the foundation itself—an immovable molar set in the jaw of the City. BAH-lahg braced both hands against the cold carved stone and leaned until the muscle stood out across his shoulders and his boots skidded on the grit underfoot.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Move,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he hissed.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statue's face remained a mask of placid indifference. It was not attacking. It was not threatening. It stood with the heavy, unthinking purpose of a shepherd's dog blocking a gap in a fence.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: It won't budge,
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo said. She leaned against the damp wall of the corridor, hollowed out by exhaustion now that the last of the adrenaline had burned off and left only the bill behind. She was still clutching the figurine, her thumb tracing the same groove across its surface over and over without seeming to know she was doing it.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We have to go through,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg growled, and backed up to try again.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We aren't going through,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said. Her voice was too steady. She was staring at the ceiling.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek followed her gaze. The joints between the stones were moving—not much, not enough to notice unless you were already looking for it—slowly, perceptibly tightening, the gaps narrowing like the ceiling itself was drawing breath.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We're being steered,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The City doesn't want us in the main colonnade anymore. It's closing the loop.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg turned from the statue.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What does that mean?

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It means the path behind us is being removed.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then we make our own path.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Through that?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun nodded at the statue.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg glanced back at it, his expression suggesting he was reconsidering several of his life's choices at once, starting with the one that had brought him to this profession.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek did not answer. He was looking at the floor instead. The dust here was different—finer, disturbed in long overlapping trails, as though thousands of feet had walked this exact path in a time that was not theirs. The compass in his pocket had stopped merely spinning; it was vibrating now, a frantic hum climbing up through his thigh and into his ribs.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Zeek?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Orders?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the statue's blank face and understood, all at once, that the City had stopped testing them. If they forced the issue now they would spend the last of their strength against something that had never needed to fight them in the first place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stepped aside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statue waited another moment, as if confirming the decision, then turned and began to walk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They followed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor it led them down was narrower than the ones they had left, the ceiling lower, the air colder. The walls here carried no incomplete spirals. They carried names.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Thousands of them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The white limestone was covered in shallow, precise cuts—row after row of personal names, some still legible, many crossed out with a single deliberate stroke. Others had been erased so thoroughly that only a pale scar remained in the stone. Ninsun slowed, stylus forgotten, eyes moving from line to line with the stricken attention of someone who had spent her life reconstructing lost records and was now watching the process run in reverse.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: These are accounts,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said quietly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Not a memorial. A ledger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg kept his axe ready.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Of what?

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: People who paid.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo's thumb stopped moving on the figurine. She looked at the wall the way she had once looked at locked doors—calculating value even when the desire for value was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek walked until he found the section that made his chest tighten.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He recognized one of the names. The characters were older than the script Ninsun had taught him, but his father had drawn them often enough in the journal that Zeek knew their shape before he understood why.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His heart gave a slow, heavy roll. He reached out before he had decided to.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The instant his fingers touched the stone the air in the chamber sharpened. A high, thin vibration filled the room—so faint at first he thought it was coming from inside his own skull—and then the sound arrived in earnest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Scrape.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pause.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Scrape.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pause.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It came from everywhere at once. The wall was not simply a record. It was active, and it had been waiting for a hand to touch it the way a trap waits for a foot.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The name beneath his fingers began to soften at the edges, the limestone rippling faintly as if it had decided, just for him, to remember what it felt like to be liquid. A fresh line cut across it—deep, precise, deliberate. Zeek pulled his hand back, but the scraping did not stop. The line kept growing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He knew that name. He had known it his whole life.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City was not carving anything new.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was erasing the old.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He leaned closer. The name was not his. Not yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was his father's.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The invisible chisel kept working. A second line crossed the first. A third crossed both. The letters disappeared beneath the cuts one stroke at a time. Ninsun's voice reached him from somewhere very far away.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Zeek?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not answer. He could hear the scraping inside his own chest now, keeping time with something that was not quite his heartbeat. The wall was erasing his father's name, methodically, patiently, the way a debt gets settled by someone who has never once in their life been in a hurry to collect.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: As the last letters vanished, ink rose in their place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not another name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A symbol.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The spiral, and the drop beneath it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's palm caught fire under the wrapped linen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The statue turned toward him. This movement was different: not directional, not procedural, but attentive. It stepped between Zeek and the wall, unhurried, deliberate, and then it knelt, lowering its massive carved head until the stone face hung level with his own. Its mouth opened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Inside was only darkness.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Out of that darkness came a voice that belonged to neither the City nor his father—a voice Zeek had never heard in his life, dry and unimpressed, like a debt collector checking a name off a very long list.

lines.speaker: The Statue
lines.text: You are late.
lines.note: Dry, flat, utterly unimpressed, like a clerk ticking a name off a long list.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark on his palm knocked once, hard, in answer.
